description: FIND-003 (fake-success: Jina HTTP-200 error/placeholder body sold as a paid digest) is substantially mitigated by the new isRealContent gate (research-product.mjs lines 48-52) — the >=300-char length floor (line 49) rejects most short Jina error stubs. But a residual fake-success path remains and is UNTESTED: (1) the error-pattern scan only inspects the FIRST 400 characters (line 50: body.slice(0,400)); a body whose real-content head is benign but whose error/placeholder/truncation notice appears after char 400 is accepted. (2) The pattern set (ERROR_BODY_RE line 47) is narrow — it matches 'rate limit/too many requests/429/error code N/"code":4/authentication is required/could not be reached' but NOT a Cloudflare/anti-bot interstitial, a JS-challenge page, a generic 'Warning: Target URL returned error 403' (no literal 'error code'), or a soft-404 navigation shell. Any such page exceeding 300 chars passes isRealContent and is returned as a paid digest. (3) Critically there is NO negative test: research-product.test.mjs has no case that feeds isRealContent an error/placeholder body and asserts rejection — the only R6 assertion (test line 31) checks the success-path digest does not contain error text, which cannot detect a gate that fails open. The rejection guarantee R6 (spec lines 28-32) is therefore unproven.
